topic.title: Agent Skills Standard
topic.docSection: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.1 Agent Skills & §5 Trigger #8
topic.summary: Progressive disclosure (name + description only at startup), solving tool bloat, SKILL.md YAML frontmatter (description required, name optional), .agents/skills/ vs ~/.gemini/config/skills/.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.1 Agent Skills | Self-Test #1 & Trigger #8 | M1L1 Slide 8
questions.q: What does an agent load into context at startup for each available Agent Skill?
options: Only each skill's name and description; the full SKILL.md is read only when the agent judges the skill relevant
The entire SKILL.md file for every installed skill
All files inside scripts/, examples/, and resources/ up front
Nothing at all until the user explicitly types a slash command
questions.why: Agent Skills use progressive disclosure: only each skill's name and description load at startup. The full SKILL.md is read only when the agent judges the skill relevant.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.1 Agent Skills | Trigger #8 | M1L1 Slide 6
questions.q: Which core problem are Agent Skills and progressive disclosure designed to solve?
options: Tool bloat, where loading hundreds of tools and rules into context makes the agent slower, costlier, and worse at picking the right one
Network latency between Cloud Run and BigQuery
Lack of encryption in third-party OAuth tokens
Container cold starts on GKE Autopilot
questions.why: Skills solve 'tool bloat'—where loading too many tools and instructions up front overwhelms the context window, increasing latency/cost and degrading tool selection accuracy.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.1 Agent Skills | Self-Test #1 & Trigger #8 | M1L1 Slide 11
questions.q: Where should a team store a PROJECT-SPECIFIC (workspace) skill so it is version-controlled and shared with the repo?
options: <project-root>/.agents/skills/<skill>/
~/.gemini/config/skills/<skill>/
/etc/google/skills/<skill>/
<project-root>/.well-known/skills/
questions.why: Project-specific (workspace) skills live at <project-root>/.agents/skills/<skill>/. Watch out for the trap offering ~/.gemini/config/skills/, which is the global path.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.1 Agent Skills | Self-Test #1 & Trigger #8 | M1L1 Slide 11
questions.q: A developer wants a custom skill to be available globally across all projects in Antigravity, the IDE, and the CLI. Where should they place it?
options: ~/.gemini/config/skills/
<project-root>/.agents/skills/
~/.config/gcloud/skills/
/usr/local/share/adk/skills/
questions.why: Global skills live at ~/.gemini/config/skills/ and work across Antigravity, the IDE, and the CLI.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.1 Agent Skills | Trigger #8 | M1L1 Slide 9
questions.q: In a skill's required SKILL.md YAML frontmatter, which field is REQUIRED and which is OPTIONAL?
options: description is required; name is optional
name is required; description is optional
Both name and version are required; description is optional
No YAML frontmatter is used in SKILL.md
questions.why: In SKILL.md YAML frontmatter, 'description' is required (since the agent uses it to judge relevance), and 'name' is optional.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.1 Agent Skills | Trigger #8 | M1L1 Slide 9
questions.q: Besides the required SKILL.md file, what optional subdirectories can an Agent Skill folder contain?
options: scripts/, examples/, and resources/
Nothing else; a skill folder can never contain anything but SKILL.md
Only compiled Docker images
Only Terraform state files
questions.why: A skill folder contains SKILL.md (required) plus optional scripts/, examples/, and resources/ directories.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.1 Agent Skills | Trigger #8 | M1L1 Slide 10
questions.q: How can an Agent Skill be activated during a session?
options: Automatically when the prompt's intent matches the skill's description, or explicitly with a slash command (/skill-name)
Only when the user explicitly types a slash command (/skill-name)
Only by restarting the agent container with a --skill flag
Only through a Cloud Scheduler cron job
questions.why: Skills activate either automatically (when the prompt's intent matches the skill's description) or explicitly via a slash command (/skill-name).

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.1 Agent Skills | Trigger #8 | M1L1 Slides 8–9
questions.q: An agent never automatically activates a newly created skill even when the user asks a relevant question. What is the most likely cause?
options: The skill's description in SKILL.md frontmatter is vague or missing the trigger keywords for that task
The user did not type the /skill-name slash command, which is mandatory for all skills
The optional scripts/ directory is empty
The skill was placed in <project-root>/.agents/skills/ instead of /tmp/
questions.why: Because the agent only sees each skill's name and description at startup, automatic activation relies on matching the prompt's intent to the YAML frontmatter description.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly lists the 5 official Agent Skill design patterns from Module 1?
options: Informational, Tool Wrapper, Generator, Reviewer, and Workflow
Sequential, Parallel, Loop, Coordinator, and Router
Prepare, Scan, Remediate, Monitor, and Audit
Span, Trace, Session, Task, and Metric
questions.why: Per §6.6 (M1L1 Slide 7), the 5 Skill Patterns are: Informational (context for an environment/task), Tool Wrapper (how to use an existing tool/CLI), Generator (content of a specific format), Reviewer (criteria to assess work), and Workflow (repeatable multi-step sequence).

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.4 Agent Registry | Trigger #13 | M2S2 Slide 19
questions.q: When a standalone skill is registered in Agent Registry, how are updates to its instructions or code versioned?
options: Through an immutable SkillRevision resource under the parent Skill and Publisher resources
By overwriting the inline Agent Card JSON file on Cloud Run
By creating a new GCP project for every version
Standalone skills cannot be versioned once created
questions.why: Standalone skills are managed, versioned, and listed through the Skill, SkillRevision, and Publisher resources in Agent Registry.
